n: This lecture is devoted to section 1.4: opioids, that is promedol, methadone, fentanyl and pethidine, and the methods of isolating them from various specimens and analysing them. Key terms: opioid, trimeperidine, methadone, fentanyl, pethidine or meperidine, cyclodol, Marquis reagent, TLC, HPLC and GC-MS. The outline: promedol, methadone, fentanyl, cyclodol, pethidine, then tramadol from the malaka material.

Promedol, that is trimeperidine, has the chemical name 1,2,5-trimethyl-4-propionyloxy-4-phenylpiperidine hydrochloride. By chemical structure it is a piperidine derivative. It is a white crystalline powder, bitter in taste, almost odourless, with a melting point of 107-108°C, synthesised in 1948. The hydrochloride dissolves well in water, partly in ethyl alcohol and chloroform, and is insoluble in diethyl ether.

Because the analgesic property of morphine leads to poisoning and morphinism, a non-narcotic analgesic was sought and more than 100 compounds were synthesised. Of these, only promedol, isopromedol, lidol and phenadone were recommended for medicine. Promedol is a first-line anti-shock agent; in pain relief it is very close to morphine, but more toxic than morphine. It is used before and after surgery and for pain relief in maternity hospitals. Remember: with frequent use, habituation is possible, as with morphine.

In poisoning with promedol, nausea, dizziness, weakness and intoxication are seen. After subcutaneous injection the effect is felt after 10-20 minutes and lasts 3-4 hours. Chemical-toxicological analysis is carried out only when there is a special instruction. It is isolated from the biological specimen with acidified alcohol or water, then extracted from the aqueous extract with chloroform at pH=6.9-8.5, giving maximum extraction.

Identification reactions of promedol. With the general precipitating reagents for alkaloids it forms precipitates of various colours. With Marquis reagent, that is H2SO4 with formaldehyde, it gives a dark red colour, with a sensitivity of 10 µg of promedol. With picric acid, through the tertiary nitrogen, a bimolecular compound of yellow colour precipitates. In TLC, methyl alcohol and glacial acetic acid 9:1 are used, a yellowish spot appears with Dragendorff reagent, and it is compared with the standard spot. In the UV spectrum in 0.1 M HCl: 251, 257 and 263 nm.

Spectral characteristics of promedol. In the UV spectrum, a solution in 0.1 M hydrochloric acid absorbs maximally at 251, 257 and 263 nm. The quantity is determined by the spectrophotometric method. It is also determined by GLC or HPLC. That is, for one substance there are several independent methods, and they confirm each other.

Methadone, with the chemical name 6-dimethylamino-4,4-diphenyl-3-heptanone, is a synthetic opioid. It was synthesised in Germany during the Second World War as a substitute for morphine. It reached clinics in the USA in 1947. Methadone base is a crystalline substance with a melting point of 76-79°C. The hydrochloride is a white crystalline substance with a melting point of 229-231°C.

Doses and use of methadone. The maximum single analgesic dose is 10 mg, and the daily dose is 30 mg. It is used as a substitute for morphine, prescribed to drug addicts in therapy, and supplied as 40 mg tablets and a 10 mg/ml solution. Its analgesic action is 5 times higher than morphine, its toxicity is lower, and its duration of action can reach 24 hours. Tolerance increases and causes physical dependence. Metabolites with narcotic action are formed, such as methadol, normethadol and acetylmethadol.

t: Table 6: substances of the methadone group
n: The sixth table lists the substances of the methadone group. Of the 16 substances in the methadone group, 15 are on List I and dextropropoxyphene is on List II. On List I are methadol, acetylmethadol, dipipanone, isomethadone, normethadone, norpipanone, phenadone and others. The table shows that methadone, phenadone and dipipanone are on List I, and dextropropoxyphene on List II.

The seventh table gives the amount of methadone in internal organs in fatal poisonings, in mg/l or mg/kg. In blood the mean is 1.0 (0.4-1.8), in brain 1.0 (0.5-1.4), in liver 3.8 (1.8-7.5), in gallbladder 7.5 (2.9-18.0). In kidneys the mean is 2.9 (1.1-6.0); source: Baselt R.C., Cravey R.H. (1995), n=1. The figures in brackets indicate the observed range.

Preliminary and colour reactions of methadone. If a 1:1 mixture of concentrated sulphuric and nitric acids is dropped on the powder, an orange colour is seen. If a 2% aqueous solution of cobalt thiocyanate is dropped on the powder, a blue colour forms. In the table: with Liebermann reagent, orange; with Mandelin, green and then light blue; with Marquis, pink-red and then fluorescent red.

We isolate methadone from specimens by the acidified alcohol or water method, then extract it from the aqueous extract with organic solvents in an alkaline medium, at pH=9-10. Methadone has 16 analogues, and they are found on the black market of drug users. For TLC, Sorbfil or Silufol is used; the systems are: cyclohexane-toluene-diethylamine 10:10:1, hexane-acetone-25% ammonia 2:2:0.2 and benzene-ethanol-diethylamine 9:1:1. With Mandelin reagent the spot changes from green to blue; in the benzene-ethanol-diethylamine 9:1:1 system, Rf=0.80.

Spectra and analogues of methadone. In the UV spectrum, a solution of methadone in sulphuric acid gives maxima at 253, 259, 264 and 292 nm. In the IR spectrum, on a KBr disc, absorption is observed in the regions of 710, 1709, 769, 1107, 943 and 1133 cm-1. In the eighth table the analogues are compared: normethadone 253, 259, 265, 292; dextropropoxyphene 252, 257, 263 and a black-violet-green colour with Marquis; dipipanone 259, 265, 293.

In 1991 a highly potent synthetic analgesic, fentanyl, appeared on the US black market in place of heroin. It is 100 times more potent than morphine and 10 times more potent than heroin, and its adverse effect on breathing is stronger. For a person weighing 70 kg the effective dose is 0.1 mg, and the effect does not exceed 30 minutes. Fentanyl has more than 100 analogues, of which 12 are found on the black market. 3-Methylfentanyl is 30 times more potent than fentanyl.

In the clinic, fentanyl is used as an intravenous anaesthetic, before and after surgery, and in cardiac surgery. Fentanyl derivatives cause, like heroin, analgesia, euphoria, constriction of the pupil and difficulty in breathing. Owing to its good solubility in fat, it reaches the brain as soon as it is taken. The duration of action, however, is not long.

The action of fentanyl analogues is similar to the opiates; they differ in onset and duration. For fentanyl the effect lasts over half an hour, for alfentanil 5 minutes. According to the table, alfentanil is ultra-short-acting, 5-10 minutes. Sufentanil is 5-10 times more potent than fentanyl. Remifentanil is the shortest-acting drug. Carfentanil has a potency 10000 times that of morphine.

Fentanyl is a lipophilic substance, that is, it is rapidly absorbed through tissues and distributed at once. In metabolism, the amide group is first hydrolysed, and it is then excreted through partial hydroxylation and the formation of glucuronides. It is isolated from specimens by the acidified alcohol or water method. From the aqueous extract it is extracted with organic solvents in an alkaline medium, at pH=7.

Colour reactions of fentanyl. With Marquis reagent: the chloroform solution is evaporated on a microscope slide and 1-2 drops are added to the residue, and an orange-coloured product forms. In the citric acid reaction, a 1% solution of citric acid in acetic anhydride is added to the residue and slowly heated on a water bath, and a red-violet product appears. For both reactions the chloroform extract obtained from the aqueous extract with an organic solvent is used.

In the TLC analysis of fentanyl, silica gel G plates, Merck, Germany, are used. When acidified iodoplatinate reagent is sprayed on, a spot forms. The systems are: first, methanol-25% ammonia 100:1.5; second, cyclohexane-toluene-diethylamine 75:15:10; third, chloroform-methanol 90:10. Fourth, ethyl acetate-methanol-25% ammonia 85:10:5; fifth, acetone; sixth, methanol; seventh, methanol-n-butanol 60:40. Eighth, chloroform-ethanol 90:10; ninth, chloroform-cyclohexane-acetic acid 40:40:20; tenth, chloroform-methanol-propionic acid 72:18:10.

The Rf values of fentanyl are given in the book's table for ten systems. In the first system, methanol-25% ammonia, Rf 0.70. In the second, cyclohexane-toluene-diethylamine, 0.43. In the third, chloroform-methanol, 0.74. In the fourth, ethyl acetate-methanol-ammonia, 0.78. In the fifth system, acetone, Rf=0.58. For systems 6-10 the values are, in order, 0.70; 0.77; 0.59; 0.08; 0.84.

Let us continue with the Rf values of fentanyl. Fifth system, acetone: Rf=0.58. Sixth, methanol: 0.70. Seventh, methanol-n-butanol 60:40: 0.77. Eighth, chloroform-ethanol 90:10: Rf=0.59. Ninth, chloroform-cyclohexane-acetic acid 40:40:20: 0.08. Tenth, chloroform-methanol-propionic acid 72:18:10: 0.84. For comparison with the standard it is more reliable to use several systems.

HPLC and GLC conditions for fentanyl. In HPLC a silica gel Spherosorb S5W column is used, 125 x 4.9 mm, 5 µm, temperature 40°C. The mobile phase is methanol containing 0.01 M ammonium perchlorate, with a UV diode detector. The retention time of fentanyl in HPLC is 0.8 minutes. In GLC: 3% SE-30 Chromosorb G-HP, glass column 2 m x 2 mm, nitrogen 45 ml/min, temperature from 100°C to 300°C, retention index RI 2720.

t: Fentanyl: UV, IR and mass spectrum
n: Spectral data of fentanyl. In the UV spectrum, a solution in 0.1 M hydrochloric acid absorbs maximally at 251, 257 and 263 nm. In the IR spectrum, on a KBr disc, absorption is observed in the regions of 1660, 701, 1493, 1263, 1273 and 1236 cm-1. In the mass spectrum, peaks are seen at m/z 245, 146, 42, 189, 44, 105, 29 and 43. The quantity is determined by GLC and HPLC.

Cyclodol is a drug that is a piperidine derivative, a white crystalline powder, poorly soluble in water and sparingly soluble in alcohol. It has an anticholinergic action and is used in treating Parkinson's disease and, together with etaperazine, chronic alcoholism. It is excreted in the urine mainly as metabolites, in part unchanged. In recent years it has begun to be used as a substance of toxicomania because of its intoxicating, stupefying and hallucinogenic properties.

Acute poisoning with cyclodol passes through 4 stages: euphoria, loss of consciousness, hallucinations, and recovery from them. The first stage develops when the therapeutic dose is exceeded 2-3 times, with 4-8 tablets; habituation develops in 1-1.5 months. Up to 30-40 tablets may be taken in a day, and without treatment painful withdrawal drags on for 7-12 days. It is often taken after acquaintance with cannabis, barbiturates and alcohol, and as doses rise, psychoses may occur.

t: Isolating cyclodol from blood and urine
n: Isolating cyclodol from blood and urine. For blood: 30 ml of 0.02 N H2SO4 is added to 10 ml of blood, brought to pH=2 with 20% H2SO4, stirred for 2 hours, centrifuged and made up to 100 ml with 0.02 N H2SO4. Then 50 ml of the mixture is brought to pH=7.5 with NaOH and extracted three times, with 10 ml each, with chloroform; the recovery is 41-43%. For urine: 50 ml of urine is acidified to pH=2 with 20% H2SO4, stirred for 2 hours, then extracted in the same way.

Identification reactions of cyclodol. With p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde, a red-pink colour forms; with Marquis reagent, light brown-violet; with Mandelin reagent, light brown-green. With the general precipitating reagents it gives precipitates of various colours and physical states. In TLC, Sorbfil or Silufol is used, with the system diethylamine-dioxane 1:490; with Dragendorff reagent by Mune, a red-brown spot forms, Rf=0.50-0.52.

Spectra and quantification of cyclodol. In the UV spectrum, a solution in 0.1 M hydrochloric acid absorbs maximally at 252, 258 and 264 nm. In the IR spectrum, on a KBr disc: 702, 756, 973, 1206, 1196 and 935 cm-1, and in the mass spectrum: m/z 98, 105, 55, 41, 99, 77, 218 and 84. The quantity is determined by UV spectrophotometry, GLC or HPLC, with a detection limit of 2 µg, and also by the extraction-photocolorimetric method with bromothymol blue.

Pethidine, that is meperidine or Demerol, was first synthesised in 1932. It is similar to morphine, but 8 times weaker and less prone to cause habituation. Pethidine base is an oily liquid of alkaline character; the hydrochloride is a white crystalline powder, boiling point 186-190°C, readily soluble in water, chloroform and ethanol. The therapeutic dose is 0.2-0.8 µg/ml, the lethal dose is 1 g, and the half-life is 2-5 hours. Taken by mouth, it acts after 15 minutes, the blood concentration peaks in 1-2 hours, and the effect lasts 1.5-3 hours.

Pethidine sometimes stimulates the central nervous system, causing tremor, muscle twitching and convulsive seizures. Paralysis of the respiratory centre is caused by its main metabolite, norpethidine. In the table the amounts of meperidine and normeperidine are given in mg/l. In blood after oral intake, 12 and 19, after intravenous injection 4.3 and 2.5. In urine after oral intake, 150 and 50, after intravenous injection 15 and 49.

Isolating pethidine. To 1 ml of blood serum, 0.1 ml of 1 M NaOH and 5 ml of hexane are added, stirred for 1 minute and centrifuged. To the centrifugate, 4 ml of solvent and 0.08 ml of 1 mmol phosphoric acid are added, and it is analysed by HPLC. The HPLC eluent is acetonitrile-phosphate buffer pH=7-methanol 55:25:20. In general it is isolated from a biological specimen with acidified water or alcohol, and extracted from the aqueous extract in an alkaline medium, pH=9-10.

Identification reactions of pethidine. With the general precipitating reagents for alkaloids it forms precipitates of various colours and physical states. With Marquis reagent it gives an orange colour, with a sensitivity of 7 µg of pethidine. In TLC, Sorbfil or Silufol is used; the systems are methanol-25% ammonia 100:1.5 and hexane:acetone:25% ammonia 2:2:0.2. With Dragendorff reagent a yellowish spot forms, and with potassium iodoplatinate a brown spot, and they are compared with the spot of the standard sample.

t: Pethidine: UV and quantification by HPLC
n: UV spectrum of pethidine and its quantification by HPLC. A solution in 0.1 M hydrochloric acid absorbs maximally at 204, 207 and 213 nm. In HPLC the column is Supercosil LC-PCN, 5 µm; the eluent is acetonitrile-phosphate buffer pH=7-methanol 55:25:20; the detector is UV at 204 nm. The detection limit is 2 ng/ml. The quantity is determined by UV spectrophotometry, GLC or HPLC.

Tramadol, as the hydrochloride, is a centrally acting synthetic analgesic, a racemic mixture of the (+) and (-) isomers. When given intravenously, analgesia develops rapidly and lasts 3-5 hours. It is weaker than morphine and at therapeutic doses hardly depresses respiration. With prolonged use, drug dependence is possible. Within 3 days about 90% of the dose is excreted in the urine, of which about 30% is unchanged; the metabolites are excreted as conjugates.

t: Isolating tramadol from urine and TLC
n: Isolating tramadol from urine and TLC. From urine at pH=11.5 it is extracted twice with equal volumes of chloroform; the extract is dried over anhydrous sodium sulphate and evaporated. The analysis is carried out on Sorbfil PTSKh-P-A-UF and KSK silica gel in four systems. The first system is toluene-acetone-ethanol-ammonia 45:45:7.5:2.5; the second ethyl acetate-methanol-ammonia 34:4:2; the third chloroform-ethyl acetate-ammonia 60:40:1; the fourth ethyl acetate-hexane-ammonia 50:15:2. The best separation is in system IV.

For tramadol the confirmatory reagent is a 1% solution of ninhydrin in concentrated H2SO4: first a pink-cherry colour forms, and after washing with water a stable orange colour. Of 54 toxicologically significant drugs, 15 gave a pink-cherry colour, but the stable orange colour after water was seen only for tramadol and Nubain. Tramadol is actively metabolised: in system IV, on Sorbfil, three additional zones corresponding to metabolites are seen, Rf x100: 12, 17, 29.

The reagents in the article's table for detecting tramadol. Dragendorff, in Moldaver's modification, gives an orange colour, minimum 1.0 µg. 0.03 M CuSO4, then KI, brown colour, 0.5 µg. Marquis reagent gives a yellow-brown colour, 3.0 and 5.0 µg. Fröhde reagent gives a blue colour, 1.0 µg. Dragendorff, CuSO4 + KI and Marquis reagent are used in general screening; Marquis and Fröhde reagents are also used in testing for the opium group.

Marquis reagent helps to distinguish opioids by colour. Promedol gives a dark red colour, with a sensitivity of 10 µg. Fentanyl and pethidine give an orange colour, with a sensitivity for pethidine of 7 µg. Methadone gives a pink-red and then a fluorescent red colour, and cyclodol a light brown-violet. Because fentanyl and pethidine give the same colour, they must be distinguished by other methods.

To conclude. Promedol, methadone, fentanyl and pethidine are synthetic opioids; they are isolated by the acidified water or alcohol method and extracted from an alkaline or neutral medium. With Marquis reagent, promedol gives a dark red colour, pethidine and fentanyl orange, and methadone pink-red. TLC, UV, IR, mass spectrum and GC-MS confirm the result. Review questions: the narcological significance of the promedol group, isolation of phenylpiperidine derivatives, and the identification of promedol, methadone, cyclodol and pethidine.

Review questions. First question: name the medicinal substances containing derivatives of the phenylpiperidine group; explain the narcological significance of promedol and the substances of this group. Second question: how are phenylpiperidine derivatives isolated from physical evidence? Third question: what chemical and physicochemical methods are used to identify promedol, methadone, cyclodol and pethidine?

Case. An unknown crystalline powder was brought to the forensic chemical examination; carry out a preliminary analysis. The solution, step by step: the appearance of the crystalline powder, then the preliminary group by colour with Marquis reagent, then in TLC the system and Rf are compared with the standard. After that it is confirmed by UV and IR spectra, and finally final identification is made by GC-MS. A second case: blood was brought, and according to the documents a substance causing hallucinations is presumed; carry out a preliminary analysis for the unknown substance.
